summary: ACCEPT V3-08 repair cycle 35679583057. Objective: REPAIR the trusted finalizer failure from Actions run 35678248910 (Android API 35 install/launch/golden-path step failed with exit 1 after 11m09s) while preserving all accepted criteria. The candidate delta is exactly one file: scripts/e2e-android.js (+16/-6). The repair fixes the interaction bug introduced by the accepted ANR repair (cycle 35672300447): waitFor() computed `const globalGraceElapsed` ONCE before its loop, so when a force-stop handler (app-ANR dismiss, crash detector, stuck detector) reset globalThis._appLaunchTime mid-loop, the stale const kept inGlobalGrace=false for the rest of the waitFor, leaving the freshly relaunched app unprotected during its new cold start. The candidate computes the global grace dynamically on each iteration ((Date.now() - globalThis._appLaunchTime) < COLD_START_GRACE_MS), so the relaunched app always receives a fresh 450s cold-start window. It also raises the post-Demarrer waitFor('Appartement') timeout from 300s to 600s: after tapping Demarrer the app performs demo sign-in + SQLite fixture seeding, the phase where the app ANR'd on degraded API 35 emulators; a force-stop + relaunch inside a 300s waitFor leaves only ~200s for the relaunched app's documented 240s cold start, guaranteeing a timeout. Independent simulation confirms: pristine 300s/const-grace → TIMEOUT after ANR at 100s; candidate 600s/dynamic-grace → SUCCESS. Trusted verification exit code 0: typecheck clean, 454 tests/22 suites pass (incl. v3-08-finalizer-wrapper 24/24), privacy release contract OK (71 tests), cost regression gate OK (21 tests), expo export android OK, prebuild OK, gradlew :app:assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 15m7s. Independent checks reproduce: node --check OK, full jest suite 454/454, cost 21/21, privacy 71/71. No product code changed: src/, app/, __tests__/, governance, directives, docs, workflows byte-identical to the pristine accepted tree. No V3-01..V3-07 invariant regressed. No must-fix remains.

findings.problem: The app-ANR force-stop + relaunch path in dismissAnrOverlay() has no recovery guard: it force-stops on every app-ANR detection regardless of how recently the last force-stop occurred. On a persistently degraded emulator the app can ANR repeatedly, and each detection cycle (dump 30-60s + force-stop + relaunch + 15s sleep) repeats until the enclosing waitFor timeout. The candidate's dynamic grace protects the relaunched app from the stuck detector but does not gate the ANR force-stop path itself.
findings.evidence: scripts/e2e-android.js lines 418-426: `if (isAppAnr) { globalThis._lastForceStopTime = Date.now(); globalThis._appLaunchTime = Date.now(); shell('am','force-stop',packageName); ... monkey ... sleep(15000); }` — no `sinceLastForceStop >= FORCE_STOP_RECOVERY_MS` guard on this path.
findings.requiredFix: None required for acceptance. The loop is bounded by the enclosing waitFor timeout (600s Appartement / 900s Demarrer) and the alternative (leaving the ANR dialog covering the app) is strictly worse. Optional hardening for a future cycle: skip the force-stop when sinceLastForceStop < FORCE_STOP_RECOVERY_MS and only tap Wait.
